newsitem.title: ITALY: Prosecutor seeks jail for Venice belltower raiders.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutor seeks jail for Venice belltower raiders.

text.p: A prosecutor on Wednesday demanded up to nine years in jail for eight separatists who stormed the belltower in Venice's St Mark's Square in a bizzare independence demonstration two months ago.

State prosecutor Rita Ugolini, summing up at a trial that began on May 21, asked that the defendants be sentenced to either eight years and two months or nine years depending on their role in the May 9 assault.
The eight, almost all in their 20s and 30s, broke into the belltower during the night after hijacking a ferry to take them and a home-made armoured vehicle to the square in the lagoon city.

Calling themselves soldiers of the "Most Serene Republic" of Venice which was for centuries a maritime power before its fall 200 years ago, the eight unfurled a flag of the republic and shouted separatist slogans.
The assault ended when police commandos stormed the landmark after about seven hours and arrested the separatists.
They were charged with kidnapping the ferry captain, subversion, illegal weapons possession, threatening public officials, and occupying church property.
Prosecutors said, however, charges relating to the armoured car had been dropped because the vehicle was not deemed capable of doing any damage.
Under Italian law, charges of kidnapping for subversive ends allow for a maximum prison sentence of 30 years.
